content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In Christian teaching, the palm of the hand (Hebrew kaph) most commonly symbolizes God's intimate, permanent remembrance and protective care of His people—the place where God 'engraves' His covenant people so they can never be forgotten. Devotionally this is frequently extended typologically to the nail-pierced palms of Christ, read as the literal fulfillment of God inscribing His people on His hands, so the palm becomes a symbol of covenant love, security, and redemptive belonging.","primary_basis":["Isaiah 49:16 ('Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands')","John 20:25–27 (the nail marks in Jesus' hands, commonly linked devotionally to Isaiah 49:16)","Isaiah 62:3 (a crown/diadem in the hand/palm of God, associated imagery of being held)","John 10:28–29 (no one able to snatch believers out of the Father's hand, often paired thematically)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The open or lifted palm as a posture and symbol of prayer, supplication, and worship—spreading or lifting the palms toward heaven.","basis":["Lamentations 2:19; 3:41 ('let us lift up our hearts with our hands/palms')","1 Kings 8:22, 38, 54 (Solomon spreading his palms toward heaven)","Psalm 63:4; Psalm 141:2 (lifting up hands in prayer)","Exodus 9:29, 33 (Moses spreading out his hands/palms to the LORD)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The palm as a symbol of one's deeds, conduct, and moral state—'clean palms' signifying innocence, or the 'work of the hands' signifying what a person has done and its recompense.","basis":["Psalm 24:4 ('clean hands and a pure heart', Hebrew kaph)","Job 16:17; Job 31:7 (no violence/spot cleaving to my palms)","Psalm 18:20, 24 (rewarded according to the cleanness of my hands)","Isaiah 59:3 (palms defiled with blood)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Striking or clapping the palm as a gesture: clapping in joy or praise, clapping in derision, or striking hands as a pledge/surety (the ancient handshake of guarantee, usually treated as a warning against rash suretyship).","basis":["Psalm 47:1; Isaiah 55:12 (clapping hands/trees clapping in joy)","Proverbs 6:1; 17:18; 22:26 (striking hands in pledge/surety)","Job 27:23; Lamentations 2:15 (clapping in scorn or derision)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The hollow of the palm as a measure of smallness or of divine immensity—God measuring the waters in the hollow of His hand, or the small cloud 'like a man's hand' signaling coming blessing.","basis":["Isaiah 40:12 (measured the waters in the hollow of his hand)","1 Kings 18:44 (a little cloud like a man's hand/palm rising from the sea)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The palm/sole (kaph is also used of the sole of the foot) as a symbol of possession and dominion—every place the sole treads being given as territory.","basis":["Joshua 1:3; Deuteronomy 11:24 (every place the sole of your foot treads)","Genesis 8:9 (the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot)"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"medium","notes":"Kaph is a broad Hebrew term (palm of hand, sole of foot, hollow/curved objects such as pans and spoons) and does not carry a single rigid symbolic code in the way terms like 'lamb' or 'leaven' do. However, within Christian preaching and devotional literature there is a clearly recognizable dominant symbolic use: Isaiah 49:16's engraving on God's palms as an image of unforgettable covenant love and security, very often connected to the nail-scarred hands of Christ. Academic biblical scholarship tends to treat kaph contextually rather than symbolically, so the 'settled consensus' applies to popular/devotional Christian interpretation more than to critical scholarship; hence confidence is rated medium rather than high."}
